svg.title: Sunset Lookout Utila: circular top terrace in plan and terrain section
svg.desc: Upper-zone plan area about 115 square metres, around twenty metres wide and five to six and a half metres deep, not a flat pad. Eighteen metre diameter circular terrace is a scale hypothesis over the downslope land. Equal-scale centreline section shows cut at rear and surface to ground gap at front; no support system is approved.

g.text: SUNSET LOOKOUT UTILA / CIRCULAR TOP-TERRACE STUDY
A plate at the top, projecting above the slope
Measured terrain context plus one 18 m diameter scale hypothesis. Relative heights use the lower path arrival as base 0 m.
Upper strip: 115 m² in plan / about 20 m across
5.1–6.5 m deep; centreline ground drops 3.3 m
TOP STRIP LIMIT / local y = 35 m
Dashed grey line: previous path; now a re-planning input
Circle stays inside the boundary in plan; margins are not approvals
SECTION A–B / DOWNHILL THROUGH THE CENTRE
18 m horizontal run / 9.2 m ground descent
The plate is level; the ground below it is not.
Rear cuts into the hillside; front projects above the falling ground.
TEST TERRACE SURFACE: +19.35 m above base
Aligned with the current model upper-path arrival, not a chosen final level.
GROUND GRADIENTS / successive 3 m horizontal intervals
Distance downhill from A; 1:1 horizontal / vertical scale
Blue line is the surface only: deck depth and supports are not designed.
Bedroom locations are PAUSED: owner intends upslope ends cut into ground and downhill ends projecting above it; future sketches/3D massing needed.
The circle overlaps earlier L2/S3 room zones and much of the upper route. It is a new organising idea, not an add-on to the previous layout.
Terrain is survey-interpolated; this is one centreline, not a geotechnical model. Above-ground projection is not a certified cantilever span.
